description: Follow-up corrections bound to exact independently confirmed old/new values and source snapshots. Source metadata is derived from reviewed fields.

oldValue: Food and treasure are not automatic escape buttons; use the pursuer's intelligence and interests.
At a three-way choice without sight, sound or scent clues, a pursuer has a two-in-three chance of taking the wrong way.
newValue: Food and treasure are not automatic escape buttons; use the pursuer's intelligence and interests.
At a three-way choice without sight, sound or scent clues, a pursuer has a two-in-three chance of taking the wrong way.

For palatable food or wine offered to pursuers of low intelligence or less, determine a 10%–100% base chance with d10 unless their hunger is known; add 10% per intelligence point below 5. Non-intelligent pursuers have a 100% probability. If the chance is under 100%, roll d10 again to test it; success distracts them for one round.

Treasure can distract pursuers of low intelligence or higher: start at 10%–100%, adding 10% per 10 items for low-intelligence pursuers or 10% per 100 gp of value or potential value for those of average intelligence or more. Test with a second d10; success lasts one round or the time needed to collect the treasure, whichever is longer. Tiny valuables can go unnoticed.
changes.reason: Add the previously deferred cited-source procedure.

oldValue: Short range uses the medium-range penalty, −2; medium range uses the long-range penalty, −5; long-range shots miss.
An unpracticed rider using those means cannot hit under this procedure.
A caster hovering with fly or a rider on a hovering flying carpet does not suffer these movement penalties; levitation has separate rules.
newValue: Short range uses the medium-range penalty, −2; medium range uses the long-range penalty, −5; long-range shots miss.
An unpracticed rider using those means cannot hit under this procedure.
A caster hovering with fly or a rider on a hovering flying carpet does not suffer these movement penalties; levitation has separate rules.
A levitating archer attacks at −1, worsening by 1 each successive round of fire to a maximum −3; a round without firing or fighting stabilizes the archer and resets the next shot to −1.
While levitating, slings, thrown javelins or spears, and swung weapons use double those penalties (−2, −4, −6). A medium or heavy crossbow cannot be cocked while levitating.

oldValue: Name-level self-study and bard contributions have separate rules.
Training must be continuous; serious interruption loses the prior time and payment.
Once eligible to advance, further XP cannot be accumulated until the new level is actually acquired.
newValue: At name level, characters train or study independently for the performance-determined time; weekly cost per level is 2,000 gp for clerics, 1,000 for fighters, 4,000 for magic-users, and 2,000 for thieves.
Training must be continuous; serious interruption loses the prior time and payment.
Once eligible to advance, further XP cannot be accumulated until the new level is actually acquired.

Bards contribute at least 50% of monetary gains plus 1,000 gp per level upon advancement to their college, through a druid able to use more of their highest-level spells than the bard; failure to pay prevents advancement. They otherwise need one week of study or training upon gaining sufficient XP.

changes.reason: Add the UA character-class table supporting the newly extracted class choices.

oldValue: Wood elves gain +1 initial strength and −1 intelligence; strength still tops out at 18.
Wild elves gain +2 initial strength to a maximum of 18 and have sharply restricted class choices.
Use the individual sub-race text and table rather than combining every elven benefit.
newValue: Gray elves share high-elf abilities, including sleep and charm resistance, sword and bow ability, infravision, secret/concealed-door detection and silent movement when alone. They share high-elf languages and add +1 to the initial Intelligence roll, up to 19.

Wood (sylvan) elves have similar elven traits, gain +1 initial Strength (maximum 18) and −1 initial Intelligence. Their starting languages are elvish, common, treant and the tongue of woodland mammals; the passage gives them no other starting languages.

Wild elves (grugach) retain standard elven resistance, weapon bonuses, infravision, silent movement and door detection. They gain +2 initial Strength (maximum 18), deal with woodland creatures as if animal friendship were in effect, and set pits, snares and natural traps with a 90% success chance. Most speak only elvish, though a player character may also know some common.

The UA p.7 class table permits gray elves to be cavaliers, clerics, druids, fighters, rangers, magic-users or thieves (including acrobats and assassins); wood elves have those choices except cavalier; wild elves can be druids, fighters or thieves (including acrobats and assassins). Wild elf multiclassing is restricted to fighter/thief.
These are the UA class choices; ability requirements, multiclass rules and the separate UA class-level limits still apply. Do not merge them with the PHB-only class limits.

newValue: Your DM may restrict available races for the campaign.

PHB class level table (U = unlimited; parenthesized entries are non-player characters only; omitted classes are unavailable to that race): dwarf fighter 9, thief U, assassin 9, cleric (8); elf fighter 7, magic-user 11, thief U, assassin 10, cleric (7); gnome fighter 6, illusionist 7, thief U, assassin 8, cleric (7); half-elf cleric 5, druid U, fighter 8, ranger 8, magic-user 8, thief U, assassin 11; halfling fighter 6, thief U, druid (6); half-orc cleric 4, fighter 10, thief 8, assassin U; human all listed classes U. All are still subject to applicable ability and class requirements.

PHB fighter limits by Strength: dwarf below 17 → 7, at 17 → 8, otherwise maximum 9; elf below 17 → 5, at 17 → 6, otherwise maximum 7; gnome below 18 → 5, otherwise 6; half-elf below 17 → 6, at 17 → 7, otherwise 8. Halfling Hairfeet and others under Strength 17 → 4; Tallfellows at 17 and Stouts at 18 → 5; Tallfellows with 18 → 6.

PHB magic-user limits by Intelligence: elf below 17 → 9, at 17 → 10, otherwise maximum 11; half-elf below 17 → 6, at 17 → 7, otherwise maximum 8. Gnome illusionists with Intelligence or Dexterity below 17 are limited to 5; with both 17 to 6; otherwise table maximum 7. Half-orc thieves with Dexterity below 17 are limited to 6, at 17 to 7, otherwise maximum 8.
The printed half-elven ranger 8 entry bears footnote 4, but that footnote explicitly describes half-elven fighters. The table’s application of that footnote to rangers is unresolved.
changes.reason: The existing card defers numeric racial class restrictions or names no PHB multiclass combinations; printed tables and descriptions supply them.
